correctness.rationale: Exact \(\(A^4=I+2B\)\) and integer-matrix squaring yield \(A^{\(2^r\)}=I+2^{r-1}B_r\). For \(r\ge3\) the binomial tail is divisible by \(2^{r+1}\); the parity of a period-four sum makes the linear remainder divisible by \(\(2^r\)\) for odd exponents, \(2^{r+1}\) for even. Every length-eight window has four odd Tribonacci terms, giving uniform \(F_{e,3}(n)\equiv4\pmod8\); for odd powers \(F_{e,3}(0)\equiv2\pmod4\). The doubling induction gives sharp orders for all scales, all powers and all starts; length 2 and 4 cases follow separately. Standalone modular checks over 24,800 windows and exact integer checks over 1,050 windows passed; the proof does not rely on them.

value.rationale: The sharp 2-adic component of a natural all-shift power-sum GCD is classified uniformly for two unbounded parameters, exhibiting a nontrivial even-versus-odd exponent split and stronger all-start exactness for even exponents. Dyadic lengths are forced by the recurrence matrix four-step parity period and its repeated squaring; the claim is not an arbitrary finite slice or a known small-table calculation. This resolves a meaningful structural feature of nonlinear Tribonacci sums and provides a reproducible lifting argument; odd factors remain unknown.
